claims.text: The transient ductile-brittle-ductile transition is driven by evolution of local chemical order within the B2 phase.
A change in FCC/B2 phase-boundary morphology or coherence during aging contributes causally to the ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
The initially weakly ordered or disordered B2 state permits easy dislocation shear and consequently high ductility.
Aging in the proposed critical range of approximately 500–650 °C produces strong LCO within the B2 domains.
The brittle state has semi-coherent FCC/B2 boundaries with high interfacial energy.
Strongly ordered B2 domains and semi-coherent phase boundaries pin dislocations and act as impenetrable barriers.
Dislocation pinning at phase boundaries produces stress localization and crack initiation, causing brittle fracture.
At higher aging temperatures, B2 coarsening, LCO relaxation, phase-boundary incoherency, or B2 transformation reduces barrier strength.
Reduced phase-boundary density or coherence restores ductility by enabling Orowan bypass or shear of ordered domains.
A continuous ordered B2 matrix is associated with high strength and low fracture strain.
The brittleness of a continuous ordered B2 matrix results from limited slip systems and high Peierls stress.
A weakly ordered BCC structure containing nanoscale B2 regions can exhibit much greater ductility than a continuous ordered B2 matrix.
An inverted microstructure consisting of a disordered continuous matrix and discrete B2 precipitates restores ductility.
The target alloy will show greater than 15% ductility in the low-LCO state, less than 5% strain in the brittle state, and greater than 10% ductility after high-temperature recovery.
Yield strength will peak in the brittle regime because LCO strengthening is maximal there.
Embrittlement occurs when the B2 LCO parameter exceeds a critical value and semi-coherent phase boundaries have misfit strain above 0.5%.
A grain-boundary embrittlement mechanism would produce crack initiation at grain boundaries without correlation to LCO or phase-boundary coherence.
The proposed mechanism predicts crack initiation at semi-coherent phase boundaries where dislocation pile-ups and maximal LCO are observed.

contradictions.description: The phase-boundary morphology is presented as a causal change into a semi-coherent brittle state, but the initially ductile state is also described as already having semi-coherent phase boundaries. Thus, phase-boundary coherence alone does not distinguish the initial ductile and brittle states as written.
